title: Hobbycast Episode 11: Video Podcast - Asian Cinema Nostalgia - Part 5
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Sq3rkK6GhuE

Part five leans hardest into Japan and Korea. Daniel (@dungeondive) opens with Takashi Miike's *Dead or Alive* trilogy, now on an Arrow Blu-ray, calling the first film's ending the most insane he has ever seen and quoting a baffling review blurb about a toilet snake. King Hu's three-hour *Legend of the Mountain*, the manga-derived *Dororo*, and *Female Prisoner Scorpion* follow, with a nod to Tarantino as the reason he tracked down so many of these.

The bootleg hall of fame gets an inductee: a copy of Oshii's *Avalon* whose sleeve credits George C. Scott and Jerry Goldsmith. *Tell Me Something* is pitched as a Korean *Seven*. *City of Lost Souls* has a ping-pong match played over swinging pendulum blades. The Godzilla section declares the 90s Heisei run his favourite, with *Godzilla vs. Mothra: Battle for Earth* at the top, and *Yokai Monsters: Spook Warfare* as the one folklore film to watch. *Ninja in the Dragon's Den* is recommended on the strength of a disco-funk theme song alone. The *Mad Mission* comedies are framed as Hong Kong's *Cannonball Run*, with entries directed by Tsui Hark and Ringo Lam. Oshii's live-action *Talking Head*, a cursed anime production seen from inside the studio, is called a masterpiece, and *Attack the Gas Station* closes the episode as a heartfelt Korean *Dog Day Afternoon*.

----

Daniel puts the Heisei Godzilla films above the originals. Which era of a long-running franchise do you defend against the consensus?
